title: harness.event.v1
description: One observation from an agent session. This layer records; it never decides. Fields for classification and enforcement are deliberately absent: they belong to a later phase and a later schema version, and reserving them here would invite the recording layer to start judging.

seq.description: Monotonic within one session. A gap means an event was lost; the loss itself is recorded out of band, never in this file.

repo_key.description: Stable repository identity (root commit, or path for a repository with no commits). Paths in this event are relative to that repository.

type.description: A checkpoint is not an event type: meta.json is the single record of what a checkpoint is, and checkpoint_ref points at it.

agent_session_id.description: The runtime's own session identifier. Several may attach to one prohairesis session.

grade.description: Adapter capability grade for the hook that produced this event (for example C3, post-execution observation). Recorded so a reader can tell how complete this record can possibly be.

kind.description: "opaque" is a first-class answer, not a failure. Collapsing an unmappable tool into a real kind manufactures the illusion of complete coverage.

command.description: argv[0] only, for exec. The rest of the command line is never stored: identity is all any metric needs, and a full command line would make this log a new place for secrets to collect.

argv_sha256.description: Digest of the full command line. Answers "is this the same command as before" without answering "what was it".

paths.description: Repository-relative where the path is inside repo_key; otherwise absolute with the home directory written as ~.

hook_ms.description: Time spent inside the hook process, excluding process start. Recorded, and deliberately not budgeted: see docs/METRICS.md.

checkpoint_ref.description: Where to start from to get back to the tree as of this event. Written on every event, not only on the ones that took a checkpoint.

taken_here.description: True when this event is the one that took that checkpoint.

truncated.description: The event exceeded the size at which it can still be written with a single write(2), so paths were dropped. Set rather than silently shortening.
